title: Aeroméxico 111
summary: An Aeroméxico Lockheed Constellation with experienced pilots departed Guadalajara at night during heavy rain on an instrument climb. The aircraft drifted from the correct course and began flying in a southwesterly direction toward Cerro Latillas mountain. The crew lost situational awareness without visual references and did not correct the navigation error. The aircraft crashed into the mountain killing all 45 occupants.
probable_cause: Spatial disorientation and loss of situational awareness due to instrument flight in poor weather and improper instrument-based navigation following takeoff.

factors.evidence: the plane was flying low and was headed into an out-of-course path
the plane kept flying straight in a south-westerly direction
Spatial disorientation and loss of situational awareness were noted by investigators
Contact with ATC was severed after no update was received and another aircraft saw a fireball coming from the ground.

events.text: Aircraft took off from Runway 28 at Guadalajara at 21:53 CST in heavy rain with night conditions
Crew halted required left turn and set aircraft to straight direction, flying southwesterly instead of climbing toward Mexico City
Contact with ATC severed as aircraft continued flying off-course path at low altitude toward mountain
Aircraft crashed into Cerro Latillas mountain

notes: exact crash location inferred from narrative

title: KLM 607-E
summary: KLM Flight 607-E, a Lockheed Super Constellation named Hugo de Groot on the second leg of a transatlantic trip from Amsterdam to New York, crashed into the Atlantic Ocean after departing Shannon Airport, Ireland, on 14 August 1958. Radio contact was lost about 35 minutes after takeoff, and a rescue operation later found light debris and recovered the remains of 34 of the 99 people aboard roughly 180 km northwest of Shannon. Irish and Dutch investigators could not pinpoint a definitive cause but believed the most likely explanation was an over-speeding outboard propeller, caused by metal particles obstructing an oil feed line regulator valve, which may have provoked a flight disturbance and caused the propeller to shear off.
probable_cause: Investigators could not determine a definitive cause but considered the most likely explanation to be a malfunctioning over-speeding outboard propeller, caused by metal particles obstructing oil feed line regulator valves, which may have provoked a flight disturbance and caused the propeller to shear off.

factors.evidence: a malfunctioning over-speeding outboard propeller caused by metal particles obstructing oil feed line regulator valves
The particles may have been formed by a gear that was damaged when the supercharger of the corresponding engine was accelerated
The malfunctions of the propeller pitch might have provoked a flight disturbance and as a consequence the propeller may have sheared off

events.text: Flight 607-E departed Shannon Airport at 03:05 UTC on the second leg of a transatlantic trip from Amsterdam to New York City, with stops in Shannon and Gander.
Radio contact with the aircraft was lost at approximately 03:40 UTC.
The investigating board believed a malfunctioning over-speeding outboard propeller, caused by metal particles obstructing oil feed line regulator valves, provoked a flight disturbance.
The propeller may have sheared off, and a rescue operation later found light debris on the ocean surface about 180 km northwest of Shannon.

notes: Cause never conclusively determined; investigators only reached a probable hypothesis after considering bomb, electrical failure and pilot error.
Flight phase at time of loss of contact is not stated in the text.
